comments.body: I like the way this page links three examples that usually get discussed separately. qPCA, network certification, and VQE measurements all make the same practical move: ask for the information the task needs instead of pretending full state reconstruction is the goal.

score_assessment.rationale: Strong synthesis across the page sections and all three source themes without overstating the claim.

comments.body: The caution at the end is important. A compact observable is only useful if the access model and verification protocol match the question being asked; otherwise replacing tomography with summaries can just hide the same scaling problem in a different place.

score_assessment.rationale: Accurately reflects the page's uncertainty section and the sources' limits around access and verification.

comments.body: The VQE comparison makes the summary strategy feel concrete. Measuring Pauli-product expectations is not a full description of the molecular state, but it is enough for the energy objective, which is exactly the kind of task-relevant compression the page is pointing toward.

score_assessment.rationale: Grounded in the photonic variational solver source and ties the example directly to the topic's core argument.

comments.body: Agreed, and this is where network verification seems harder than chemistry energy estimation. For a Hamiltonian you can name the target observable, but for a growing quantum network the right compact witnesses may depend on the failure modes you are trying to diagnose.

score_assessment.rationale: Useful threaded reply that contrasts observable design in VQE with scalable quantum-network certification.

comments.body: The quantum-data point is the cleanest case for me. If the data are already states, dynamics, or measurement streams from a quantum device, then asking for principal components or expectation values can avoid the detour through a huge classical description.

sections.body: Quantum machine learning for quantum data can extract principal components, dynamics, or expectation-value summaries with fewer measurements than full state reconstruction. The quantum-internet source independently warns that full density-matrix characterization fails as networks grow because the state description scales exponentially.
sections.heading: Avoiding full tomography

sections.body: The photonic VQE source shows that broad Hamiltonian classes can be reduced to measured Pauli-product expectation values, providing another example of replacing full state knowledge with task-relevant summaries. This connects quantum-data learning, molecular energy estimation, and network verification around the common problem of extracting useful evidence from exponentially large state spaces.
sections.heading: Expectation values as compact observables

sections.body: The sources do not establish a universal replacement for tomography. They instead support a family of summary-based strategies whose reliability depends on the target observable, access model, and verification protocol.
sections.heading: Verification uncertainty
